panels.title: Uptime - History
panels.description: Historical uptime for each server. After a server restarts, its uptime returns close to zero. Historical data is available from the moment Prometheus started collecting metrics.

One row per server; horizontally displayed Uptime gauge with automatic scaling. A visible status legend appears below and in this info tooltip. Hover over the Notes cell tooltip indicator (Grafana 12.2+) for details. 'Restarted in range' means at least one uptime reset detected in the selected time window; restarts are estimates from Prometheus samples, not system events. The Uptime gauge uses field-specific min/max so reboot timestamps do not distort the bar scale.

properties.value: See status legend below the table. Hover over the Notes cell for detailed status explanation on Grafana 12.2+.

0.text: OFFLINE: server is stopped (uptime 0). No reset detected within the selected time range.

1.text: ONLINE: server is running. No uptime reset detected within the selected time range.

2.text: OFFLINE + RESET: server is currently stopped, but at least one uptime decrease or reset was detected within the selected time range.

3.text: RESTARTED IN RANGE: server is online now; at least one uptime reset was detected in the selected Grafana period (e.g., last 24 hours). This is an estimate; restarts between scrapes can be missed.

panels.title: Uptime - Summary

options.content:
**Notes legend:** 🟢 **Online** = running · 🔴 **Offline** = stopped  
🟠 **Restarted in range** = reset in selected period · 🟠 **Offline · reset detected** = stopped now, reset in period

targets.expr: (pterodactyl_server_cpu_absolute{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} * on (server_name, id, job, instance) group_left (cpu_limit) (label_replace(label_replace(count_values by (server_name, id, job, instance) ("cpu_limit", pterodactyl_server_max_cpu_absolute{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} @ end()), "cpu_limit", "$1%", "cpu_limit", "^(.+)$"), "cpu_limit", "unlimited", "cpu_limit", "^0%$") > bool 0)) or on (server_name, id, job, instance) label_replace(pterodactyl_server_cpu_absolute{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"}, "cpu_limit", "unavailable", "server_name", ".*")

panels.title: CPU usage / limit
panels.description: One row and line per server. Last shows CPU usage (e.g. 240%), with the limit in the legend (e.g. 500%). Unlimited servers (limit 0) are included as 'unlimited'; usage remains visible if the limit metric is missing. The limit is taken at the end of the selected time range.

panels.title: CPU usage percent
panels.description: Percentage of the configured CPU limit in use (absolute usage / limit × 100): for example, 200% out of 400% = 50%. No value for servers with unlimited CPU (limit 0).

targets.expr:
(pterodactyl_server_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} * on (server_name, id, job, instance) group_left (memory_limit) ((label_replace(count_values by (server_name, id, job, instance) ("memory_limit", round((pterodactyl_server_max_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} @ end() >= 0 and pterodactyl_server_max_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} @ end() < 1024), 0.1)), "memory_limit", "$1 MiB", "memory_limit", "^(.+)$")
    or
    label_replace(count_values by (server_name, id, job, instance) ("memory_limit", round((pterodactyl_server_max_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} @ end() >= 1024 and pterodactyl_server_max_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} @ end() < 1048576) / 1024, 0.1)), "memory_limit", "$1 GiB", "memory_limit", "^(.+)$")
    or
    label_replace(count_values by (server_name, id, job, instance) ("memory_limit", round((pterodactyl_server_max_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} @ end() >= 1048576 and pterodactyl_server_max_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} @ end() < 1073741824) / 1048576, 0.1)), "memory_limit", "$1 TiB", "memory_limit", "^(.+)$")
    or
    label_replace(count_values by (server_name, id, job, instance) ("memory_limit", round((pterodactyl_server_max_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} @ end() >= 1073741824) / 1073741824, 0.1)), "memory_limit", "$1 PiB", "memory_limit", "^(.+)$")
    or
    label_replace(count_values by (server_name, id, job, instance) ("memory_limit", (pterodactyl_server_max_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"} @ end() == 0)), "memory_limit", "unlimited", "memory_limit", "^0$")) > bool 0)) or on (server_name, id, job, instance) label_replace(pterodactyl_server_memory_mebibyte{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"}, "memory_limit", "unavailable", "server_name", ".*")

panels.title: Memory usage / limit
panels.description: One curve and legend row per server: used memory in the graph and Last column, configured limit in the legend (0 = unlimited). Values use binary units automatically (MiB/GiB/TiB).

panels.title: Disk usage / limit
panels.description: One curve and legend row per server: used disk space in the graph and Last column, configured limit in the legend (0 = unlimited). Values use binary units automatically (MiB/GiB/TiB).

panels.title: Network Traffic RX - Current (bit/s)
panels.description: Average inbound network speed per server over the last 5 minutes; SI bit/s with automatic kbps/Mbps/Gbps scaling.

panels.title: Network Traffic TX - Current (bit/s)
panels.description: Average outbound network speed per server over the last 5 minutes; SI bit/s with automatic kbps/Mbps/Gbps scaling.

panels.title: Network Traffic RX / TX - Current (bit/s)
panels.description: Inbound (RX) and outbound (TX) speeds as two separate series per server, averaged over the last 5 minutes; SI bit/s with automatic kbps/Mbps/Gbps scaling.

panels.title: Network RX - Cumulative
panels.description: Cumulative inbound traffic per server, shown in bytes with binary scaling with automatic MiB/GiB/TiB/PiB scaling.

panels.title: Network TX - Cumulative
panels.description: Cumulative outbound traffic per server, shown in bytes with binary scaling with automatic MiB/GiB/TiB/PiB scaling.

panels.title: Network RX / TX - Cumulative
panels.description: Cumulative RX and TX traffic: two separate series per server, shown in bytes with binary scaling with automatic MiB/GiB/TiB/PiB scaling.

panels.title: Network Traffic - Current (bit/s)
panels.description: Total, RX and TX network throughput across the selected servers, averaged over 5 minutes (SI bits/s, automatically shown as kbps/Mbps/Gbps).

panels.title: Network Traffic - Cumulative
panels.description: Total, RX and TX traffic since the latest game-server counter resets across the selected servers, displayed as automatically scaled IEC bytes (MiB/GiB/TiB). Each direction can reset on a server restart.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (id) (pterodactyl_server_backup_count{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"}) / clamp_min(max by (id) (pterodactyl_server_backup_limit{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"}), 1) and on (id) (max by (id) (pterodactyl_server_backup_limit{server_name=~"$server",panel=~"$panel"}) > 0)

panels.title: Backup - Last Backup and Limits
panels.description: Latest backup, backup usage, and full UUID for each server. A limit of 0 means backups are disabled; negative limits (if supported by the provider) are displayed as unlimited.
